page: Google Cloud Platform m2-ultramem-208 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for massive in-memory computing requirements. It features 208 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 104 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.7 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES. Memory capacity is the defining specification of this platform, supplying 5,888.0 GB (5.75 TB) of RAM, which equates to 28.31 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, no GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate specialized aggregate scale alongside low per-core throughput. In multi-threaded execution, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (183,859.54) and PassMark extended instructions (164,000.11), bolstered by strong uncached memory bandwidth of 321.2 GB/sec read and 149.33 GB/sec write. In-memory data structures perform exceptionally well, demonstrated by 147.67 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect the lower base clock and older core architecture, resulting in weak single-core stress-ng (1343.99) and Geekbench (961.0) scores, along with subpar single-thread compression speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m2-ultramem-208 represents a highly consolidated infrastructure investment. It optimizes footprint and licensing overhead for enterprise systems that cannot be horizontally partitioned across smaller instances, trading per-core compute efficiency for enormous unified memory addressability. Hardware tradeoffs involve the total reliance on external network-attached block storage for persistence and constrained single-thread execution latency.

The instance is best matched with enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis deployments, large-scale graph databases, and extensive memory-resident data analytics that require contiguous terabyte-scale RAM alongside high-thread multi-core concurrency.
